thread.title: Facebook Shareholders Brace For Zuckerberg Testimony In Congress

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Facebook Shareholders Brace For Zuckerberg Testimony In Congress

organizations.name: facebook shareholders brace for zuckerberg testimony in congress facebook

text:
Facebook ( FB ) Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg needs to win over Republican lawmakers when he testifies before two congressional panels next week on data privacy issues in the wake of the Cambridge Analytica scandal, says an analyst.
X "CEOs don't win hearings, they just hope to survive and not make comments that fuel calls for punishment and regulation," Paul Gallant, regulatory analyst at Cowen & Co., said in a note to clients.
Facebook stock has plunged 14% since the Cambridge Analytica scandal broke in March. But the sell-off in Facebook shares has eased the past few days as shareholders brace themselves for Zuckerberg's testimony. Gallant says the hearings could draw "Watergate"-type audiences on the TV and internet.
Facebook lost 1.3% to 157.20 amid broad market selling on the stock market today .

Please contact customer service CLOSE Zuckerberg is set to appear before a joint hearing of the Senate Judiciary and Commerce committees on Tuesday afternoon, followed by a House Energy and Commerce hearing on Wednesday.
The Federal Trade Commission is investigating Facebook's possible noncompliance with a 2012 consent decree on consumer privacy protection.
"The Republican party has touted its light-touch policy toward internet/tech companies as enabling the emergence and global leadership of Apple ( AAPL ), ( Alphabet's ( GOOGL )) Google and Facebook and others," Gallant said. "That hands-off philosophy is now being tested. If Republicans go hard at Zuckerberg and call for new privacy limits, we believe that will encourage the FTC to be more aggressive toward Facebook and perhaps Google, Twitter ( TWTR ), Snap ( SNAP ) and other ad-based internet companies. It also would increase prospects for Congress to pass privacy legislation in the next couple of years."
Zuckerberg has also been summoned to appear in front of lawmakers in the U.K. and European Union.
In a recent interview with Vox, Zuckerberg said he's open to independent oversight of Facebook's editorial decisions and content management policies.
Sheryl Sandberg, Facebook's chief operating officer, on Friday told NBC that Facebook users would have to pay to use the social network if they completely opt out of their data being used to target them with advertising.
